title: Bhutan Sikkim and Darjeeling Tour Package
highlights: Explore ancient dzongs, lush valleys, and Himalayan landscapes on a Bhutan, Sikkim & Darjeeling tour rich in culture, history, and natural beauty.
Marvel at the awe-inspiring 177-ft Buddha Dordenma Statue in Bhutan, one of the tallest Buddha statues globally, offering breathtaking vistas of the Thimphu Valley.
Make your way to Tiger’s Nest (Taktsang) Monastery, standing 10,240 feet high above Paro, Bhutan where the legend speaks of Guru Rinpoche flying on the back of a tigress.
Stand in awe of the enchanting beauty of Tsomgo Lake, Gangtok, a serene glacial lake famed for its stunning vistas, as you traverse the landscape for breathtaking views of Mt. Kanchenjunga.
Ascend to Tiger Hill in Darjeeling, a renowned viewpoint that rewards visitors with views of the world’s highest peaks, including Mount Everest and Kanchenjunga.
overview:
About the destinations:
Bhutan: Known for its untouched landscapes and rich Buddhist culture, Bhutan is a must-visit for nature lovers and spiritual seekers. Key attractions include the Paro Taktsang (Tiger’s Nest), perched on a cliffside, and the Punakha Dzong, a stunning fortress. Bhutan is also perfect for trekkers, with trails like the Druk Path offering views of snow-clad peaks. Ideal for those looking for a peaceful, immersive experience, it’s often included in Darjeeling Sikkim Bhutan tour packages for a well-rounded journey.
Gangtok: This vibrant capital of Sikkim is surrounded by the Himalayas and offers panoramic views, particularly of Mount Kanchenjunga. Gangtok is a hub for adventure activities like trekking, river rafting, and paragliding. Don't miss the sacred Rumtek Monastery or the Tsomgo Lake, a high-altitude glacial lake. For culture and nature enthusiasts, it’s an ideal stop in Bhutan Sikkim Darjeeling tour, offering a blend of modern amenities and traditional charm.
Darjeeling: Famous for its tea gardens and panoramic views of Mount Kanchenjunga, Darjeeling is a serene hill station ideal for honeymooners, families, and nature lovers. A ride on the Darjeeling Himalayan Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, offers a nostalgic experience. Tiger Hill is a popular spot to catch the sunrise over the Himalayas. Included in many Darjeeling Sikkim Bhutan tour packages, Darjeeling is a charming and laid-back destination with colonial-era architecture and scenic beauty.

know_before_you_go: Images are for representation purpose only.

ID proof is mandatory for each individual guest at the time of booking, and upon arrival. PAN Card will not be considered as a valid identity proof. All foreign nationals must carry their passport as a proof of identity.

Indians must pay the Sustainable Development Fee (SDF) of Rs 1200 per person/per night. Children below 5 years are exempted from SDF, while kids between 6 and 12 years of age, will get 50% concession.
To obtain entry in Bhutan, Indian tourists must carry their passports with a minimum 6 months validity and make the payment of SDF.
Plastic has been banned since 1999 in Bhutan, therefore, it is advised to carry plastic/plastic items.
Keep your arms and legs covered while visiting a Dzong (fortress-monastery).
Travellers aren't expected to wear the traditional kira, but you should make sure your clothing covers your arms and legs when entering a Dzong.
Ask for permission from the attending authority before taking any photos or videos inside places like monasteries.
In Bhutan, Tuesday is ‘Dry Day’. This means locals don’t drink alcohol on Tuesday. So it would be respectful to avoid alcohol on Tuesdays too.
It’s illegal for tobacco to be sold in Bhutan. Tourists can bring cigarettes into the country, but can only smoke them in designated places.
Bhutan does not have a micro (or nano) SIM card. So check your mobile device for SIM compatibility before visiting Bhutan.
Ask your local guide to help you purchase a SIM on arrival, as Bhutan supports 2 networks: B-Mobile SIM and TashiCell.
Credit cards are widely accepted in major cities and tourist areas. However, it is recommended to carry some cash.
The official currency in Bhutan is the Bhutanese Ngultrum (BTN). It is advisable to exchange currency at banks or authorised exchange bureaus.

Please note that prices are dynamic and may change in the peak season and on blackout dates.
Any breakage or damage of any items in the stay property will be charged at actuals.
Please note that the timings and duration of pick-up and drop-off transfers may vary based on certain factors like traffic, weather conditions, natural calamities, etc.
Prices may fluctuate with any change in services/hotels. The difference in the cost shall be borne by the client in case of any amendment in the package due to an increase in the number of guests.

If in case any traveller wants to or decides to leave the trip in the middle, all the expenses from the point onwards will be borne by the traveller. Neither the operator nor Thrillophilia will be held responsible for such decisions or for any refund.
Please note that on Saturdays and Sundays, the Phuntsholing Bhutan permit office remains closed.
It is recommended that you purchase travel insurance for your Bhutan Sikkim Darjeeling tour. Please note that the travel insurance is not included in the package price.
Please note, the provided vehicle is for point-to-point services only. Any extra usage beyond the itinerary will incur additional charges, payable in cash on the spot.

meal_plans.name: Bermuda Plan
meal_plans.description: The Bermuda meal plan offers three meals at select restaurants, including breakfast, lunch, and dinner along with drinks included. Ideal for a hassle-free, all-inclusive dining experience.

meal_plans.name: Dinner Plan
meal_plans.description: The Dinner Plan provides guests with two meals included in their stay: breakfast and dinner.

meal_plans.name: American Plan
meal_plans.description: It includes all three major meals, breakfast, lunch, and dinner for the length of your stay. Generally, the rates on this plan are higher but offer a good value for your money, and of course, added convenience.

meal_plans.name: Modified American Plan
meal_plans.description: Also known as Half Board or Half Pension meal plan. It is a modified version of the American Plan and includes a room stay with breakfast and a choice between lunch and dinner.

meal_plans.name: Continental Plan
meal_plans.description: It is where your room stay involves a daily breakfast at the hotel. The hotel can either affix its option of breakfast menu or provide in the dining area for a buffet breakfast. Also, whether the room service provides the breakfast or in a general dining area, depends from hotel to hotel.

meal_plans.name: European Plan
meal_plans.description: Only the stay is included in the rates and that you will have to pay extra for using the hotel’s dining facilities. This can be called the “Room Only” Plan.

days.title: Arrival in Siliguri | Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: Welcome to Siliguri! Upon arrival at the Bagdogra Airport/NJP Railway Station, marks the beginning of your Bhutan Sikkim Darjeeling Tour.​ From there, get driven to the vibrant border town of Phuntsholing. After checking in, spend the rest of your day at leisure, where you can visit the Amo Chhu Crocodile Breeding Centre to see endangered species like the alligator up close, or take a peaceful walk along the picturesque Torsa River. Also, you can explore the town’s bustling local markets.

days.title: Transfer to Thimphu | Leisure Day
days.desc: Post check-out, visit the immigration office in Phuntsholing to obtain a travel permit. Then, enjoy a scenic drive to Thimphu. Upon arrival, check in to your hotel and spend the rest of your day at leisure. You can head out and visit Simply Bhutan, an interactive museum. Also, you can visit the National Institute for Zorig Chusum, where students perfect Bhutan’s 13 traditional arts, or explore the Clock Tower Square, where you can sample authentic Bhutanese cuisine.

days.title: Thimphu Sightseeing Tour | Transfer to Paro
days.desc: After checking out, begin your Thimphu sightseeing with a visit to the National Memorial Chorten, a revered stupa adorned with intricate religious sculptures. Next, marvel at the 177-foot-tall Buddha Dordenma, one of the largest Buddha statues in the world, overlooking Thimphu Valley. Continue to the Motithang Takin Preserve, where you can spot the takin, Bhutan's unique national animal. Later, get driven to Paro and check in at the hotel for a comfortable overnight stay.

days.title: Visit to Ta Dzong & Rinpung Dzong | Tiger's Nest Monastery Trek
days.desc: Today, visit the Ta Dzong, once a strategic watchtower and now a museum showcasing a vast collection of Bhutanese artefacts. Explore the Paro Rinpung Dzong, a historic fortress that boasts intricate woodwork. Later, embark on a trek from Satsam Chencho Tshongkhang to the Taktsang Monastery, situated on a cliff at 3,120 metres. As you hike through dense pine forests, soak in the amazing views. At the Monastery, explore sacred meditation caves and ancient murals dedicated to Guru Rinpoche.

days.title: Transfer to Phuntsholing | Leisure Day
days.desc: After checking out, get driven to Phuntsholing. Upon arrival, check in and spend the rest of your day at leisure. You can head out and visit the Gumpha Mandir, which offers peaceful views of the surroundings. Next, you can visit the Tashi Chholing Shedra, a respected monastic school where monks study Buddhist teachings. Also, you can explore the vibrant Phuntsholing Market, famous for its local handicrafts and produce.

days.title: Transfer to Gangtok | Leisure Day
days.desc: Today, enjoy a scenic journey to Gangtok, known for its pristine landscapes. After checking in at the hotel, spend the rest of your day at leisure, where you can relax or explore the city on your own. You can visit the Phodong Monastery, dating back to the 18th century, renowned for its vibrant murals and religious significance. Also, you can stroll through Lal Bazaar, bustling with local crafts, spices, and street food.

days.title: Gangtok Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, embark on a sightseeing tour of Gangtok sightseeing tour and visit the Tashi Viewpoint, offering stunning views of the Mt.Kanchenjunga Ranges. Next, pay a visit to Ganesh Tok and Hanuman Tok before heading to the Directorate of Handicrafts & Handloom and the Institute of Tibetology. Later, soak in the peaceful ambiance of chantings at Dro-Dul Chorten Monastery and marvel at the powerful cascade of the  Ban Jhakri Falls, Lhasa, and Bakthang Waterfalls. Later, get driven to your hotel.

days.title: Gangtok Excursion Tour
days.desc: In the morning, head to the stunning Tsomgo Lake, or Changu Lake, at an altitude of 3,753 metres. This glacial lake is known for its seasonal colour change, from deep blue in summer to frozen white in winter. Next, visit the Baba Harbhajan Singh Temple, a shrine dedicated to Indian army hero Baba Harbhajan Singh, believed to protect soldiers in the region. For a thrilling experience, visit Nathula Pass (14,140 feet), where India meets China on the ancient Silk Route. Later, return to the hotel.

days.title: Transfer to Darjeeling | Leisure Day
days.desc: After checking out, enjoy a scenic transfer to Darjeeling. Upon arrival, check in and spend the rest of the day at leisure, where you can stroll through Nightingale Park, a peaceful spot with manicured lawns and mountain views. Also, you can visit St. Andrew’s Church, built in 1843, a testament to Darjeeling’s colonial past or head to Mahakal Mandir, a sacred Hindu shrine. You can also walk up to Observatory Hill for breathtaking views of the Kanchenjunga range.

days.title: Darjeeling Sightseeing Tour
days.desc: Today, embark on a full-day Darjeeling sightseeing tour. Start with an early morning ascent to Tiger Hill (2,590m) to witness the sunrise over Mt. Kanchenjunga, the third-highest peak in the world. Next, visit the Batasia Loop, a spiralling railway track offering stunning panoramic views of Darjeeling’s landscape, followed by the ancient Ghoom Monastery, home to a 15-foot Maitreya Buddha statue. Also, witness the rare Red Pandas at Darjeeling Zoo, before getting driven to your hotel.

days.title: Departure Day
days.desc: It’s time to bid farewell to Darjeeling as your Bhutan Sikkim and Darjeeling Tour​ comes to an end. After checking out of the hotel, board your transfer to Bagdogra Railway Station/Airport. As you depart, take with you cherished memories of Bhutan’s serene monasteries, Sikkim’s stunning landscapes, and Darjeeling’s natural charm—sights and experiences that will stay with you forever. Safe travels!
